To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
mevalonate decarboxylases are reduced in the liver of SHRSP from two weeks of the age.
the amount of mevalonat pyrophosphate decaboxylase (MPd) was reduced in the brain and liver of the stroke-prone spontaneously hyperensive rat (SHRS) from two weeks of life.
mevalonate decarboxylate in the liver and brain of stroke-prone spontaneously hypertension rat is reduced at two weeks old.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of reduced mevalonate pathway enzyme in SHRSP.
the mechanism of reduced amount of MPDs in SHRSP.
the identification of the molecular mechanism underlying the reduced MPD in SHR, and the elucidation of the relationship between the MPD and the hypertension.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MPD in liver and brain of SHRSP is significantly reduced from the age 2 weeks.
MPD in liver and brain of SHRSP is reduced from the early age.
the amount of MPD protein in SHRSP is reduced from two weeks old, but not in the brain and liver.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the reduction of MPD in brain and liver of SHRSP may be related to the development of hypertension in SHRSP.
MPD in SHR liver is reduced at two weeks of age and that the reduced amount of liver MPD is not related to the hypertension of the SHRSP.
the reduction of MPD in the brain and liver from 2 weeks of age may be one of the factors for the development of hypertension and stroke in SHRSP.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the amount of MPD is reduced from the young age in SHRSP.
the reduced amount of mevalonolactone in the brain is the cause of the reduced amount of squalene in the brain.
the reduced amount of mevalonolactone in SHRSP liver is not due to the reduced amount of liver MPD.
